newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul slaps travel ban on bank heads over Hanbo.
newsitem.headline: Seoul slaps travel ban on bank heads over Hanbo.

text.p: South Korea on Tuesday banned the heads of four main creditor banks of Hanbo Steel Co from leaving the country in connection with a probe into loans to the steelmaker, a Justice Ministry official said.

The four banks are Korea First Bank, Cho Hung Bank, Korea Exchange Bank and unlisted Korea Development Bank, which have the biggest exposure to Hanbo Steel, flagship of Hanbo Group, the official said.
"The government today imposed an overseas travel ban on a further 17 people, including the heads of the four banks, over the Hanbo investigation," he told Reuters.

This brings to 29 the total number of people banned from leaving the country because of the Hanbo's loan scandal, he addded. Others include Hanbo Group founder, Chung Tae-soo, and other Hanbo executives.
Hanbo Steel, which defaulted on debts last week, borrowed five trillion won ($5.8 billion) from 61 banks and financial institutions, about 20 times its net worth, according to the finance ministry.
